message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where you’ll put the code |
|--------|-----------------|---------------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (or a CI job) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/instances` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, SDK, etc.) |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud calls its VM product “Compute Engine”, not “EC2” (that’s AWS).  
> *The RTX A6000 is available as the accelerator type `nvidia-a6000`.  
> *You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and a **GPU‑enabled quota** in the chosen zone.  
> *After the instance starts you’ll need to install the NVIDIA driver (the startup‑script below does that automatically).*

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE="n1-standard-8"      # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-a6000,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --metadata install-nvidia-driver=true \
  --tags http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### `startup.sh` – install the NVIDIA driver

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install the NVIDIA driver (recommended version for A6000)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot so the driver loads (optional – you can also just load it)
# reboot
```

> **Tip** – If you want the instance to stay up after the script finishes, remove the `reboot` line or add `sleep 60` before it.

---

## 2. REST API (curl example)

> **Prerequisites**  
> *You need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.*

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
TOKEN="ya29.a0AfH6SM..."   # <-- your OAuth token

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" },
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

> **What the JSON does**  
> * `machineType` – 8‑vCPU, 30 GB RAM.  
> * `guestAccelerators` – one RTX A6000.  
> * `disks` – 100 GB SSD boot disk from the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.  
> * `metadata` – tells the instance to install the NVIDIA driver and runs a small startup script.  
> * `tags` – open HTTP/HTTPS ports (adjust as needed).  
> * `serviceAccounts` – gives the VM full Cloud Platform access.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-a6000` in chosen zone |
| ✅ | `gcloud auth login` (or OAuth token) |
| ✅ | `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=$ZONE` shows `nvidia-a6000` |
| ✅ | Instance will install NVIDIA driver automatically |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@$INSTANCE_IP
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy GPU computing!
